title: Tohoku Earthquake and Tsunami
summary: On 11 March 2011 a great thrust earthquake on the Japan Trench, off the northeast coast of Honshu, generated a tsunami that reached the coast within 30 minutes and overtopped seawalls. NOAA reports over 18,000 dead, and the tsunami disabled three Fukushima Daiichi reactors. Magnitude is given as 9.0 or 9.1 depending on source.

uncertainty.note: Sources disagree on magnitude (9.0 vs 9.1), not on date.

where.modern_name: Off the east coast of Honshu, Japan (epicentre)
where.historical_name: Offshore northeast Honshu, Japan; Pacific coast of Tohoku region

importance.justification: Largest earthquake recorded in Japan, with a deadly tsunami and the Fukushima Daiichi accident; NOAA calls it the most expensive natural disaster in history.

audience_note: Concerns a disaster with many thousands of deaths, including victims never recovered.

related.because: The tsunami disabled power and cooling at three Fukushima Daiichi reactors.
